title: Annihilator of a finite module commutes with localization at an element
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $f\in A$, and $M$ a finitely generated $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], with annihilator $\operatorname{Ann}_A(M)=\{a\in A: am=0\text{ for all }m\in M\}$. Let $A_f$ be the localization of $A$ at $f$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] and $M_f$ the localization of $M$ at $f$, an $A_f$-module [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. Then $\operatorname{Ann}_{A_f}(M_f)=\operatorname{Ann}_A(M)A_f$, the ideal of $A_f$ generated by the elements $a/1$, $a\in\operatorname{Ann}_A(M)$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 07T8 (algebra-lemma-annihilator-flat-base-change), second assertion, for the flat ring map A -> A_f (Algebra, Lemma 00HT algebra-lemma-flat-localization), with M (x)_A A_f = M_f; its proof uses Lemma 0BBY (algebra-lemma-flat-intersect-ideals). This special case is the 'algebra fact' that the proof of Morphisms, Lemma 05JU (morphisms-lemma-scheme-theoretic-support) states and omits.
